title: Proof starts with three products of our own
lede: Bloop is in build and piloting in Bologna. Washiiba is built end to end. Kerf is a case study on public data. Every build runs on one repeatable spine, proven on our own products. Client work follows as it ships.

items.name: Bloop
items.kind: Own product · in build, piloting in Bologna
items.oneLiner: An AI events concierge for Bologna.
items.summary: We are building Bloop and piloting it in Bologna. You chat in plain language and it proposes real events from a live catalogue.
items.tagline: An AI events concierge for Bologna.
items.built: A chat concierge over a live catalogue of events. You ask in plain language and it proposes real events from that catalogue. Italian first, with English, and a web admin for curating the catalogue.
items.proves: We can build a conversational AI product that answers from live data.

items.name: Washiiba
items.kind: Own product · built end to end
items.oneLiner: A complete laundry marketplace, mobile and web from one codebase.
items.summary: A laundry marketplace built end to end. Customer flows for ordering, pickup windows and live order status, an admin backend, and web and mobile from a single codebase.
items.tagline: A laundry marketplace on web and mobile from one codebase.
items.built: Customer flows with ordering, pickup windows and live order status, plus an admin backend, on web and mobile from a single codebase.
items.proves: We can build a full marketplace across web and mobile, end to end.

items.name: Kerf
items.kind: Own product · case study on public data
items.oneLiner: Overhead-line vegetation clearance, ranked from free national LiDAR.
items.summary: Kerf turns free national LiDAR (IGN LiDAR HD in France) into a ranked list of overhead-line spans where vegetation is inside the clearance zone, measured in metres, then a work order for trimming crews. It is made for small electricity distributors and vegetation management contractors.
items.tagline: From free national LiDAR to a work order for trimming crews.
items.built: A LiDAR processing pipeline, a web map viewer with the ranked span list and per-span measurements, work order export (CSV) and a printable report. The case-study run covers 345 spans on 28.4 km of overhead line: 829.5 million LiDAR points, scanned in June 2021, processed in 83 seconds on one server.
items.proves: We can take raw public data to a ranked, measured result and a work order. Kerf is a case study on public data and is not yet validated in the field.
